2027-04-08.title: Second Thursday of Resurrection
2027-04-08.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: The privilege of believing in Christ and suffering for him
The faith of the Canaanite woman
2027-04-08.alt: Season of the Resurrection (Qyamta). The Queen of Heaven (Regina Caeli) is prayed in place of the Angelus until Pentecost.
2027-04-08.verse: Then Jesus answered her, “Woman, great is your faith! Let it be done for you as you wish.” And her daughter was healed instantly.
theo: Paul writes to the Philippians from prison, not knowing whether he will live or die. He does not ask them to get him released. He asks for something harder: “Only, live your life in a manner worthy of the gospel of Christ.” The Greek word Paul uses means to live as a citizen; Philippi was a Roman colony, proud of its citizenship, and Paul tells them that they belong to a greater city, and must live by its laws. A Christian's daily conduct is the visible face of the Gospel. Paul hopes to hear “that you are standing firm in one spirit, striving side by side with one mind for the faith of the gospel, and are in no way intimidated by your opponents.” Then he says something no one could invent: “For he has graciously granted you the privilege not only of believing in Christ, but of suffering for him as well.” Suffering for Christ is called a gift of grace, a privilege, like faith itself. The apostles in Jerusalem had understood this when, after being flogged, “they rejoiced that they were considered worthy to suffer dishonor for the sake of the name” (Acts 5:41). Easter does not remove the Cross from the Christian life; it changes its meaning. Those who suffer with the Risen Lord share his victory.

In the Gospel Jesus goes north into the district of Tyre and Sidon, outside the land of Israel. A woman comes out to meet him, and Matthew calls her a Canaanite, using the oldest name for the peoples who lived in the land before Israel: she is as much an outsider as anyone could be. Yet her first words are a confession of faith: “Have mercy on me, Lord, Son of David; my daughter is tormented by a demon.” What follows is one of the hardest scenes in the Gospels. “But he did not answer her at all.” The disciples want her sent away. Jesus says he was sent “only to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.” She will not go. “But she came and knelt before him, saying, ‘Lord, help me.’” Three words, one of the shortest prayers in the Bible and perhaps the most prayed. Jesus answers with a proverb that sounds harsh: “It is not fair to take the children's food and throw it to the dogs.” And she, with a mother's courage and quick wit, turns his own words into her plea: “Yes, Lord, yet even the dogs eat the crumbs that fall from their masters' table.”

“Then Jesus answered her, ‘Woman, great is your faith! Let it be done for you as you wish.’ And her daughter was healed instantly.” Only twice in Matthew's Gospel does Jesus single out someone's faith for such praise, and both times the person is a Gentile: the centurion at Capernaum and this Canaanite mother. The silence and the hard words were not rejection; they drew out of her a faith that grew stronger with every refusal. The Fathers saw in her the whole Gentile world, waiting at the edge of Israel's table for the bread of life, and receiving not crumbs but the whole loaf. After the Resurrection the Lord will send his apostles to “make disciples of all nations” (Matthew 28:19); the Gospel came to India with Saint Thomas, and the Church of the Saint Thomas Christians is one of the fruits of that mission. Every Holy Qurbana is that table: the children's bread is now given to all who come in faith. And every mother who has prayed for years for a sick or wandering child can stand beside this woman. God's silence is not his absence. Keep kneeling; keep saying, Lord, help me.
conn: “They rejoiced that they were considered worthy to suffer dishonor for the sake of the name” (Acts 5:41); “Blessed are you when people revile you and persecute you” (Matthew 5:11).
“But our citizenship is in heaven, and it is from there that we are expecting a Savior, the Lord Jesus Christ” (Philippians 3:20).
“Be strong and courageous; do not be frightened or dismayed, for the LORD your God is with you wherever you go” (Joshua 1:9).
Ruth the Moabite says, “your people shall be my people, and your God my God” (Ruth 1:16); she became an ancestor of David and of Christ (Matthew 1:5).
Jesus says of the centurion, “in no one in Israel have I found such faith” (Matthew 8:10).
The Risen Lord sends the eleven: “Go therefore and make disciples of all nations” (Matthew 28:19).
altar: At the Holy Qurbana we are all given the children's bread: not crumbs from the table but the Body and Blood of the Lord himself, given to all who come in faith and humility.
Before Holy Communion we pray in our own words what the Canaanite mother prayed: we are not worthy, yet we trust in his mercy. Lord, help me.
outline: A prisoner who asks not for release but for a worthy life.
Silence, refusal and a mother who will not leave.
Children's bread for all the nations.
A mother kneeling at the back of a church, night after night, for her child.
live: Choose one area of daily conduct, at work or online, where your behaviour does not yet match the Gospel, and change it.
Unite one pain or humiliation this week to the Cross of Christ, and offer it for someone.
Pray one of the shortest prayers (Matthew 15:25)
Whenever you are anxious this week, say: Lord, help me.
Pray daily this week for a child, your own or another's, who is sick or far from God.
fathers: To suffer for Christ is a greater gift than to raise the dead or to work miracles. When I work a miracle I am in debt to Christ; when I suffer for Christ, he counts himself in my debt. That is why Paul calls suffering a grace that has been given to you.

She did not take offence when she was called a dog. She said, Yes, Lord. By humbly accepting what she was, she was made what she was not: from a dog she became a daughter. Humility opened the door that pride would have shut.
magis: Jesus already answers prayer during his ministry, hearing the prayer of faith expressed in words, as with the leper, Jairus, the Canaanite woman and the good thief.
Everyone is called to enter the Kingdom; first announced to the children of Israel, it is meant to welcome people of all nations.
The Cross is the unique sacrifice of Christ, yet he calls his disciples to take up their cross and follow him, associating them with his redeeming sacrifice.
Martyrdom is the supreme witness given to the truth of the faith; the martyr bears witness to Christ who died and rose.
saints: Monday 5 to Saturday 10 April: the second week of the Resurrection. Sunday 11 April: the Third Sunday of Resurrection. The Latin Church keeps the Annunciation of the Lord on Monday 5 April this year (moved from 25 March, which fell on Pesaha Thursday); Syro-Malabar faithful follow the direction of their eparchy.
2027-04-08.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, Son of David, risen Saviour of all nations, you heard the cry of the Canaanite mother and praised her great faith. Have mercy on us, and help us. Give us her humility and her perseverance, so that we do not give up when you seem silent. Make us live in a manner worthy of your Gospel, standing firm together and unafraid, and count it a grace to suffer for your name. Feed us at your table with the bread of your children, and send us to all who wait for it. Glory to you, with the Father and the Holy Spirit, for ever. Amen. Alleluia!

quick: Paul: Live your life in a manner worthy of the gospel of Christ.
Suffering for Christ is a privilege granted like faith itself.
The Canaanite mother: Lord, help me. Jesus: Woman, great is your faith!
2027-04-08.action: Every time you feel anxious today, pray: Lord, help me.
2027-04-08.question: Do I give up praying when God seems silent?
catechism: Jesus hears the prayer of faith.
kidsaint: St Monica's son Augustine did not believe in Jesus and lived a wrong life. For many years Monica prayed and cried for him every day. She never gave up. At last Augustine became a Christian, a bishop and a great saint! Lesson: like the mother in today's Gospel, never stop praying for the people you love.
term: The old name for the peoples who lived in the land before Israel. Mark calls this woman a Syrophoenician; Matthew calls her a Canaanite to show that she is a complete outsider to Israel. Her great faith shows that the Gospel is for every nation.

family.explain: A mother came to Jesus because her daughter was very sick. At first Jesus did not answer. But she did not give up. She knelt down and said, ‘Lord, help me!’ Jesus was so happy with her faith that he healed her daughter. When we pray, we should keep trusting Jesus, even when we have to wait.
family.intention: We pray for children who are sick, and for their mothers and fathers.
family.ask: Ask: “What is something we have been praying for? Let us not give up!”

illus: For three years a Hindu mother from a village near Kottayam came every Tuesday evening to a small church and sat quietly at the back. Her daughter had a serious illness, and the doctors had little hope. She did not know the prayers, but she would fold her hands and say in Malayalam, ‘Help me.’ The sacristan, who had been asked many times by others why she was allowed to stay, always answered, ‘Jesus never sent a mother away.’ When her daughter recovered enough to go back to college, the mother brought a garland of jasmine and laid it before the crucifix, wept, and went home. She still comes on Tuesdays, she says, to say thank you.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on us. We come to you as the Canaanite mother came, kneeling and trusting. Help us. Amen. Alleluia!
share: Live your life in a manner worthy of the gospel of Christ (Philippians 1:27). Where does my conduct not yet match the Gospel?
He has graciously granted you the privilege… of suffering for him (Philippians 1:29). How can I offer a present suffering to Christ?
But he did not answer her at all (Matthew 15:23). How do I respond when God seems silent?
Woman, great is your faith! (Matthew 15:28). Whom do I need to keep praying for?
interc: For Christians who suffer for their faith, that they may stand firm and be unafraid.
For mothers and fathers who pray for sick or wandering children, that they may not lose heart.
For people of other religions who seek God with a sincere heart.
For the mission of the Church to all nations, in the footsteps of Saint Thomas.
For ourselves, that we may live in a manner worthy of the Gospel.
pm.close: Father, your Son heard the cry of a mother from a foreign land and praised her faith. Give us that faith which does not give up, and feed us at the table of your children. Through Christ our Lord. Amen. Alleluia!

homily: Dear friends, Paul writes from prison, not knowing if he will live. He does not ask the Philippians to get him out. He asks: live your life in a manner worthy of the gospel of Christ.

Our daily behaviour is the visible face of the Gospel. And Paul says something surprising: God has granted you the privilege not only of believing in Christ, but of suffering for him. After Easter the Cross remains, but it has a new meaning. Those who suffer with the Risen Lord share his victory.
In the Gospel a Canaanite woman, a complete outsider, cries out: Have mercy on me, Lord, Son of David; my daughter is tormented by a demon. Jesus does not answer. The disciples want her sent away.
But she kneels and says: Lord, help me. When Jesus speaks of the children's bread, she answers: Yet even the dogs eat the crumbs that fall from their masters' table. She will not give up.

Jesus says: Woman, great is your faith! And her daughter is healed. His silence drew out a greater faith. And now, at the Holy Qurbana, the children's bread is given to all who come in faith, from every nation.
If you have been praying a long time for a child or for someone you love, stand beside this mother. God's silence is not his absence. Keep kneeling. Keep saying: Lord, help me. Alleluia! Amen.
kids: Children, a mother came to Jesus because her little girl was sick. Jesus did not answer at first, but she kept asking: ‘Lord, help me!’ And Jesus healed her daughter.
When you pray and nothing seems to happen, don't stop! Keep saying: ‘Jesus, help me.’ He always hears you.

concl: The Risen Lord turns suffering into grace and silence into deeper faith.
His table is open to every nation; let us come to it with humble, persevering faith.
2027-04-08.resolve: This week, change one habit unworthy of the Gospel, offer one suffering, and pray ‘Lord, help me’ without giving up.
